title: Environmental Aspects and Impacts Register
purpose: Lists the environmental aspects of the organisation's activities, products and services that it can control or influence, their actual or potential impacts under normal, abnormal and emergency conditions, which are significant and why, and the controls in place.

questions.text: Which of these areas apply to the organisation's activities, products or services? Tick only what applies — each ticked area becomes a confirmed starting point for the register; add anything else under Other.

items.label: Clearing of native vegetation
items.note: clearing is controlled under the Environmental Protection Act 1986 (WA)

items.label: Emissions or discharges to air, land or water (for example dust, fumes, run-off)
items.note: pollution and environmental harm under the Environmental Protection Act 1986 (WA)

items.label: Controlled waste (for example waste oil, solvents, some batteries) — storage, transport and disposal
Land that is or may be contaminated (for example old fuel or transformer areas)
Storage and handling of dangerous goods (for example fuels, gases)
Refrigerants and other synthetic greenhouse gases (for example air-conditioning; gas-insulated switchgear)
Energy use and greenhouse gas emissions (fuel, electricity)
items.note: national reporting applies above the Act's thresholds

items.label: Threatened species, ecological communities or heritage places of national significance near the work
Climate change — conditions that affect the organisation, or that its activities affect

questions.text: How does the organisation decide which aspects are significant (criteria and scoring)?
Which abnormal or emergency conditions should be considered (for example spills, fires, equipment failure)?

requiredSections: Register of aspects and impacts (normal, abnormal and emergency conditions)
Controls and links to compliance obligations
expectedRecords: Management review minutes reviewing significant aspects
draftingRules: Table columns: ID | Activity, product or service | Aspect | Impact | Condition (normal / abnormal / emergency) | Significance score | Significant? | Controls | Linked obligation.
Build rows only from the ticked areas, the confirmed profile and the answers. Where nothing is confirmed, leave a placeholder row — never invent aspects or impacts.
Name an instrument only where its area is ticked or it appears among the confirmed obligations.
reviewerChecklist: Every row traces to a confirmed activity or area
Abnormal and emergency conditions are covered
Significant aspects have controls and owners
Linked obligations are real and current

brandingInstructions: Use the organisation's confirmed legal or trading name in the header, its logo reference (describe where the logo goes — do not invent one) and its confirmed brand colours for headings and table header rows. Put the document-control block in the footer or on a cover table. If a branding value is not confirmed, leave a placeholder.
